I have always found the idea of New Year's resolutions a little strange.
I think we've attached too much importance to the idea of a fresh start.
We make ambitious promises to ourselves when motivation is high, only to abandon them when everyday life inevitably gets in the way.
And when we miss a day, skip a workout, or fall back into an old habit, we often consider the entire resolution a failure.
For a while I assumed that was a me problem.
Then I looked at when we're all supposed to start.
You've just spent two weeks eating and sitting and staying up late, and your sleep is wrecked.
Your bank account is recovering.
The house is still half-full of decorations and leftovers.
Everyone you work with is coming back groggy and behind, so the week is a scramble.
Mostly I've stopped expecting the first of January to mean anything, and that's been fine.
The things I've actually changed in my life started whenever they started, for reasons that had nothing to do with fireworks.
